name: Private credit stress
summary: Non-traded BDC redemption requests still exceed quarterly caps; no forced sales or bank spillover
state: Redemption requests at non-traded BDCs, including Blackstone's BCRED, have run well above the usual 5% quarterly caps, and requests now exceed new fundraising (InvestmentNews; Bloomberg Government). Gates remain in force at several funds. No forced asset sales or losses spreading to banks or insurers had been reported as of 6 Nov.
for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit funds may face limits on how much they can withdraw each quarter. Wider bank and insurer exposure has not shown stress.
rubric_hit: Watch: large funds limiting redemptions; no simultaneous gating with forced sales or spillover to banks

sources.title: InvestmentNews — Blackstone BDC redemption surge signals a warning for other funds
Bloomberg Government — Private credit BDC redemptions exceed fundraising for first time

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
